skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray series showing rapid progression from bilateral opacities to dense consolidations followed by complete radiological resolution within a short timeframe (e.g., two weeks).
steps: Compare the initial imaging (showing bilateral opacities) with subsequent images demonstrating rapid evolution into dense, confluent consolidations.
Verify the presence of complete or near-complete radiological clearance in follow-up imaging obtained within a short interval (approx. 2 weeks).

Correlate this specific temporal pattern—rapid worsening to consolidation followed by swift resolution—with alveolar hemorrhage syndromes (such as Weil Syndrome/Leptospirosis), distinguishing it from bacterial pneumonia (which typically resolves slower and requires antibiotics) or viral pneumonias (which often leave residual interstitial markings).
